lun-wenxu-congee.title: The Number One Scholar's Congee
lun-wenxu-congee.subtitle: Lun Wenxu · A Bowl of Congee, as the Legend Goes
lun-wenxu-congee.quote: Even a bowl of congee can have its day in the sun.
lun-wenxu-congee.intro: You run a congee shop. Every day before dawn, a skinny young lad stands at your door, breathing in the smell of congee.

lun-1.title: The Lad at the Door
lun-1.text: The young man is Lun Wenxu. His family is poor and he can't afford a bowl. You watch his eyes fix on the pork liver and pork sausage simmering in the pot.

lun-2a.title: A Bowl of Congee
lun-2a.text: Lun Wenxu finishes the congee and writes you a shop sign: "Number One Scholar Congee." You laugh at him: "Think you're guaranteed to top the imperial exam?"

lun-2b.title: Congee for Dishwashing
lun-2b.text: Lun Wenxu washes the dishes and recites his books at the same time. Hearing him reel it off without a stumble, you think: this lad is something else.

lun-3a.title: The Results Are Posted
lun-3a.text: Years later, Lun Wenxu takes first place in the imperial exam. He comes back to the congee shop and writes out "Number One Scholar Congee" in his own hand.
lun-3a.endingText: Even a bowl of congee can have its day in the sun.

lun-3b.title: No Sign Left
lun-3b.text: After he rises high, Lun Wenxu returns to thank you. You tell him the sign rotted away long ago; laughing, he writes a fresh one.
lun-3b.endingText: Good congee fears no deep alley, and a good man fears no humble origins.

lun-1: Give him a bowl for free
Ask him to wash dishes in exchange for congee
lun-2b: Set aside a bowl for him every day
Introduce him to a private school

及第.note: "Jidi" marks the highest honour in the old exams.

放榜.meaning: to post the list of successful candidates
放榜.note: In imperial times, rankings were posted publicly.

chen-mengji-trick.title: The Trickery of Chen Mengji
chen-mengji-trick.subtitle: Chen Mengji · The Legend of Xinhui's Scheming Advisor
chen-mengji-trick.quote: Scheming isn't about hurting people — it's about helping the little guy get a fair shake.
chen-mengji-trick.intro: You're a farmer in a village in Xinhui. The landlord has raised the rent and you can't pay. Word is there's a man in town, Chen Mengji, famous for cooking up schemes.

chen-1.title: Finding Chen Mengji at the Teahouse
chen-1.text: Chen Mengji sits in the teahouse, fanning himself. He hears you out, then smiles: "This scheme needs you to play your part."

chen-2a.title: Playing Ghost
chen-2a.text: Chen Mengji tells you to wear white and wander before the landlord's ancestral graves at midnight. The next day the landlord turns green with fright.

chen-2b.title: The Fake Official
chen-2b.text: Chen Mengji tells you to pose as a government runner, claiming the landlord has overcharged rent and must be audited. The landlord's guilty conscience does the rest — the rent drops on the spot.

chen-3a.title: The Landlord Concedes
chen-3a.text: The landlord cuts the rent and even compensates in rice. Chen Mengji says: "Hearsay isn't always true — but the people's anger is."
chen-3a.endingText: Hearsay isn't always true, but the people's anger is.

chen-3b.title: Quit While You're Ahead
chen-3b.text: You back off, and Chen Mengji doesn't blame you. Later the landlord cuts the rent himself, calling it "storing up good karma."
chen-3b.endingText: Sometimes you don't need a scheme — time will do the work for you.

chen-2b: Hold on to the fake token

扭计.meaning: to scheme, to plot a way out
扭计.note: In Cantonese, often a clever plan that turns the tables.

摇住把扇.note: The classic look of an old-time legal advisor.

祖坟.note: Held in deep respect in the old days.

官差.note: In the old days they collected grain taxes and handled cases.

心虚.note: Said of someone who has done wrong.

赔米.note: Grain was a common form of payment back then.

积阴德.note: An old saying urging people to do good.

zhuji-xiang-south.title: Night at Zhuji Lane
zhuji-xiang-south.subtitle: Zhuji Lane · A Great Migration, as the Legend Goes
zhuji-xiang-south.quote: Leaving wasn't out of fear — it was so we could keep on living.
zhuji-xiang-south.intro: In the last years of the Southern Song, word spreads through Zhuji Lane: soldiers are coming to put everyone to the sword. You're a young man in the lane, and tonight you must decide whether to go.
zhuji-xiang-south.type: Legend / Hearsay · Roots of the Cantonese

zhuji-1.title: Torches at the Lane's Mouth
zhuji-1.text: In the middle of the night, torches flare at the mouth of the lane. Luo Gui, a tribute student, gathers everyone and says they must cut bamboo and lash rafts overnight, then sail south down the Zhen River.

zhuji-2a.title: Rafts on the Water
zhuji-2a.text: Along with 33 clans and 97 households, you shove the rafts into the river. Consort Hu is among the crowd too, and no one knows what lies ahead.

zhuji-2b.title: The Empty Lane
zhuji-2b.text: You stay. The next day the lane is so quiet it's frightening. Your neighbours all left overnight — only a few chickens remain.

zhuji-3a.title: The Pearl River Delta
zhuji-3a.text: The rafts drift downstream, and you reach the Pearl River Delta. Later generations would call Zhuji Lane "the hometown of seven hundred years ago."
zhuji-3a.endingText: Leaving wasn't out of fear — it was so we could keep on living.

zhuji-3b.title: The Names Left Behind
zhuji-3b.text: You stay and write down everything that happened in the lane in a ledger. Years later, the migrants' descendants come back to trace their roots, and the ledger becomes proof.
zhuji-3b.endingText: Some leave, some stay — either way, so the story has someone to remember it.

zhuji-1: Stay and see how it plays out

贡生.meaning: tribute student, a scholar selected for the imperial academy
贡生.note: Luo Gui is the legendary leader of the Zhuji Lane migration.

结筏.note: A means of travel by water.

胡妃.note: A figure tied to the Zhuji Lane migration legend; versions differ.

前路.note: Here, the future of the migration.

桑梓.note: The ancients planted mulberry and catalpa by their homes; the trees came to mean "hometown."

寻根.note: Zhuji Lane is the root of many Cantonese clans.

boluo-festival.title: The Boluo Chicken
boluo-festival.subtitle: Miaotou Village · The Legend of a Paper Chicken
boluo-festival.quote: The Boluo chicken — it all hangs on the glue.
boluo-festival.intro: In the second lunar month, Miaotou Village in Huangpu is packed shoulder to shoulder. You squeeze into the Temple of the South China Sea and see stall after stall of Boluo chickens — paper birds in red and green.

boluo-1.title: Market Day at Miaotou
boluo-1.text: On the main day of the Boluo Festival, Miaotou Village is so crowded you can't move. You see an old man at a stall with rows of paper Boluo chickens, their combs red enough to shine. He says: "Young fella, buy one — it's good luck."

boluo-2a.title: Where the Paper Chicken Comes From
boluo-2a.text: Gluing on feathers as he talks, the old man says: "They say a merchant from the land of Boluo once came to the temple, bringing two chickens. In the end he never left — he stayed at the temple."

boluo-2b.title: Daxi Sikong
boluo-2b.text: The old man lowers his voice: "The merchant was called Daxi Sikong. He stared toward his homeland until he turned to stone. The villagers took pity on him and made paper chickens to honour him."

boluo-3a.title: The Stone Statue in the Temple
boluo-3a.text: You step into the temple and see a stone statue with its face turned toward the sea. Incense smoke is thick, and Boluo chickens are piled before it. Some press their palms together; others just stand quietly a while.
boluo-3a.endingText: A paper chicken, offered to a man who never made it home.

boluo-3b.title: Taking a Chicken Home
boluo-3b.text: You buy a Boluo chicken and the old man ties it up with red string. Back home, your mother laughs: "A Boluo chicken — it's all held together by glue." You laugh too, but you don't call her out.
boluo-3b.endingText: Some stories only stay alive because they stick.

boluo-1: Ask the old man why it's called that
boluo-2a: Ask what became of the two chickens
boluo-2b: Go see the stone statue in the temple
Buy a chicken and take it home

好意头.note: Cantonese speakers care a great deal about "yih tau" (auspiciousness).

黐.note: Pronounced "chi1"; it also means to latch onto someone and not leave.

听讲.note: Storytellers use it to introduce hearsay.

香火.note: Thick incense smoke means many worshippers.

靠黐.meaning: to rely on glue; also to sponge off others
靠黐.note: The double meaning in the saying "Boluo chicken — held by glue."

拆穿.meaning: to see through, to call out
拆穿.note: Cantonese says "tear off the foreign mirror" for exposing a trick.

thirteen-factories-silver.title: The Silver Chest of the Thirteen Factories
thirteen-factories-silver.subtitle: The Thirteen Factories · The Legend of a Silver Chest
thirteen-factories-silver.quote: Silver can be lost; a good name can't.
thirteen-factories-silver.intro: You're a clerk at the Thirteen Factories trading houses. Tonight you must escort a silver chest down to the boat, and the manager says: don't ask what's inside.

silver-1.title: The Manager's Chest
silver-1.text: After closing, the manager calls you into the counting room. On the desk sits a wooden chest bound in iron, its lock brand new. He says: "Tonight you escort it alone."

silver-2a.title: Eyes on the Wharf
silver-2a.text: You shoulder the chest and walk the long corridor of the trading house. Behind the pillars, someone keeps following you. You quicken your step; so do the footsteps behind.

silver-2b.title: What You Shouldn't Know
silver-2b.text: The manager stares at you a moment, then lowers his voice: "It isn't silver inside. It's a stack of ledgers." Your heart sinks — you know this chest is heavier than silver.

silver-3.title: Night Fog on the Pearl River
silver-3.text: Fog rises over the wharf, and the river slaps the stone steps. The pickup boat hasn't come. Suddenly a drop seeps from the corner of the chest — not like water, sticky to the touch. You sniff it: salty.

silver-4.title: The Names in the Ledger
silver-4.text: You pry open a crack and see a stack of ledger pages. At the top are a dozen names — and one of them is your father's. Your hand jerks, and the lid snaps shut with a clap.

silver-5a.title: One Page Missing
silver-5a.text: You pull out a single page and stuff it in your pocket. The boat arrives, and you hand over the chest. You glance back: the manager stands under the arcade, as if he saw everything.

silver-5b.title: The Sealed Chest
silver-5b.text: You hand the chest over exactly as it was, without a word extra. The manager pats your shoulder: "Young man, you know how to play it." But inside, you'll remember that name.

silver-e1.title: Ending · Staying at the Trading House
silver-e1.text: You stay, rising from clerk to comprador. Years later, you donate that page to the merchants' guild with one sentence: "Black on white — don't burn it."
silver-e1.endingText: Silver can be lost; a good name can't.

silver-e2.title: Ending · The One Who Left
silver-e2.text: You take a boat out that night; no one knows where you go. Years later, a great fire sweeps the Thirteen Factories and many ledgers burn to ash. When you hear the news, you only touch the page in your pocket.
silver-e2.endingText: Some ledgers can be burned away; some names cannot.

silver-2a: Duck into an alley and shake him off
Stop and turn to confront him
silver-2b: Refuse and tell him to find someone else
silver-3: Open the chest for a look
Act as if nothing happened and wait for the boat
silver-4: Leave it untouched and escort it
silver-5a: Pretend you know nothing and report back
Leave the Thirteen Factories that very night
silver-5b: Quit and never touch it again

十三行.meaning: the Thirteen Factories, Qing-era Guangzhou's foreign trade houses
十三行.note: The old site is in today's Liwan, Guangzhou.

商馆.note: In the Thirteen Factories era, these clustered along the Pearl River.

账.note: The most sensitive thing in any trading house.

接应.note: Common in old smuggling and escort work.

撬开.note: To force open with a tool.

识做.meaning: to know how to behave, to be sensible

买办.meaning: comprador, a middleman for foreign trade
买办.note: A key role in the Thirteen Factories era.

whampoa-foreigner.title: The Foreigner of Whampoa Old Port
whampoa-foreigner.subtitle: Whampoa Old Port · The Legend of a Pocket Watch
whampoa-foreigner.quote: Not everyone who comes from the sea is a thief, and not everyone waiting on shore is a good man.
whampoa-foreigner.intro: You're a boatman at Whampoa Old Port. Late at night, a foreign merchant asks you to take him out to his ship and gives you a pocket watch as a deposit.

whampoa-1.title: The Late-Night Customer
whampoa-1.text: The old port has closed for the day, only a few lamps left on the wharf. A tall, blond foreigner stands on the jetty, a silver pocket watch in his hand, gazing at the river.

whampoa-2a.title: A Watch as Deposit
whampoa-2a.text: The foreigner tosses you the watch. The lid springs open — inside isn't a clock face, but a tiny photograph: a Chinese woman and a shopfront.

whampoa-2b.title: Where To
whampoa-2b.text: In broken Cantonese the foreigner says: "To the big ship, before daybreak." You look at the river — the ship is far out, and the fog is thick.

whampoa-3.title: The Patrol Boat Mid-River
whampoa-3.text: Mid-river, a light flares ahead — a government patrol boat. The foreigner instantly ducks low and stuffs the watch into your pocket.

whampoa-4a.title: The Runner's Question
whampoa-4a.text: The runner asks: "How many aboard?" You say two. He lifts his lamp into the cabin; the foreigner has covered himself with a straw mat, only the tips of his shoes showing.

whampoa-4b.title: Dead End in the Side Channel
whampoa-4b.text: The channel narrows the further you row, until a sluice gate blocks the way. You realise you've been led into a trap; behind you, the patrol boat has already followed in.

whampoa-5.title: The Foreigner's Story
whampoa-5.text: Once you're clear, the foreigner tells the truth: the woman in the photo is his wife, and his partner swallowed up the shop. He's come back only to retrieve a deed.

whampoa-6.title: Lights of the Thirteen Factories
whampoa-6.text: Before dawn, you feel your way into the back alley of the Thirteen Factories. The shop's sign has changed, but the stone steps are as they were. The foreigner stands in the shadows, hands shaking too much to open the lock.

whampoa-e1.title: Ending · An Old Deed
whampoa-e1.text: When the door opens, the foreigner takes only one yellowed deed and doesn't touch a single coin of the rest. At daybreak he boards his ship and leaves, leaving the pocket watch with you.
whampoa-e1.endingText: Not everyone who comes from the sea is a thief, and not everyone waiting on shore is a good man.

whampoa-e2.title: Ending · After Daybreak
whampoa-e2.text: You tell him to come back at daylight. The next day the shop is emptied out, and the foreigner never appears again. Years later, you still keep that pocket watch; the photo inside the lid smiles very quietly.
whampoa-e2.endingText: Some people leave, and only then does anyone remember they were ever here.

whampoa-2a: Snap it shut and mind your own business
whampoa-2b: Set off before the fog lifts
Bring along a second pair of hands
whampoa-4b: Abandon the boat and go ashore
whampoa-5: Trust him and see it through
Take the money, don't ask questions
whampoa-6: Tell him to come back at daylight

番鬼.meaning: old slang for a foreigner, "fan kwai"
番鬼.note: A period term; not something to say to someone's face today.

黄埔古港.meaning: Whampoa Old Port, Guangzhou's old foreign-trade harbour
黄埔古港.note: A key customs port in the Qing dynasty.

表盖.meaning: the lid of a pocket watch

半咸淡.note: Said of Cantonese spoken with a strong accent.

艇舱.note: Small boats had space in the middle to hide things.

横涌.note: Common in the Pearl River Delta's waterways.
